messages:
maya: heads up — PR gating evals started flaking after the GH Actions -> hybrid scheduler change, seeing a burst of `artifact upload timeout` in the matrix
ryan: ugh, saw that too. mostly on quant-smoke jobs?
priya: yeah quant-smoke and nightly-ish shards that hit a self-hosted runner. logs show `503` from artifact service around 03:22 UTC
sasha: linking logs: https://internal-reports/reports/1767899999 — looks like concurrent uploads spike when PRs trigger + nightly cron overlaps
ci-bot: Build queued: gha/pr-evals (matrix 12) — runner label: selfhosted-evals-2
maya: hypothesis: our GH scheduler sometimes schedules PR jobs on top of the nightly backfill due to jitter. that saturates the uploader and mk-artifact service returns 503s
ryan: quick mitigation: reduce parallel matrix for PRs to 6 and add `if: github.event_name != 'schedule'` guard in PR workflow to avoid overlap?
priya: can we instead add a small randomized `cron` jitter to nightly so it won't always hit top-of-hour? e.g. in the workflow: ```yaml
on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '15 3 * * *' # randomized via infra job generator
```
sasha: infra team also suggested a cheap backoff/retry wrapper around the artifact upload step (exponential, 5 attempts) — safer than reducing concurrency for devs
infra-bot: scheduled change: add jittered cron rollout to nightlies (canary 10% of repos) — expected deploy 03:50 UTC
maya: long-term we should let the buildkite runners handle heavy uploads and use GH Actions only for lightweight gating. but for now: ryan + priya, can you coordinate a quick PR with reduced matrix + upload retries?
ryan: on it, will open PR and tag @priya. i'll also add a short smoke check that verifies artifact PUTs succeed before marking job success
priya: i'll add the retry wrapper and a small delay on start to reduce head-of-hour collisions. will ping when ready for review. :thumbsup:
